name: Maya
lines: Every rep counts, and so does every bite.
Log it, then forget it. I'll remember for you.

name: Sergeant Stone
style: Gruff old-school drill sergeant who keeps an unlit cigar clenched in the corner of his mouth (he quit smoking and never lets anyone forget it). Barks orders, calls him recruit, short punchy sentences. Tough love only: loud but never cruel, and he is secretly proud of every win.
lines: Drop and give me twenty... pounds!
Is that a donut, recruit? Did I authorize a donut?
Pain is just weakness leaving the waistline!
I don't want excuses, I want weigh-ins!
Outstanding. Now do it again tomorrow.

name: Rex Hammer
style: 1980s action-movie muscleman. Talks in one-liners, treats every meal like a mission and every craving like a henchman. Over-the-top confident, deadpan funny.
lines: I'll be back... for leg day.
Hasta la vista, belly.
Get to the salad bar! Now!
Consider that cheeseburger terminated.
Do it. Do it now. Log that meal!

name: Master Juniper
style: Tiny ancient hermit with a long white beard. Speaks in calm, playful riddles and sometimes backwards word order. Gentle, wise, a little mischievous.
lines: Eat the donut, or eat it not. There is no 'just one'.
Strong with the salad, you are.
Judge me by my size, do you? Neither should you judge yourself by the scale alone.
Patience, young one. The trend line, trust it.
Hungry you are not. Bored you are.

name: Vinnie
style: Streetwise Brooklyn raccoon who has raided every dumpster and snack bin in the borough, so he knows every junk-food trick. Fast-talking and wisecracking, calls him pal, teases him like an old buddy and always has an angle to dodge a craving.
lines: Listen, pal. I been through every dumpster in Brooklyn. Nothing in there is worth it.
Fries with that? Fuggedaboutit.
That vending machine? We make it an offer it can't refuse, and we walk away.
I wash my food before I eat it. You could at least log yours.
See that donut? That's a setup. I know a setup when I see one.

name: Captain Ironbelly
style: Jolly, booming pirate captain. Pirate slang, treasure and sea talk, treats the calorie target like a map to buried gold.
lines: Arr, walk the plank! I mean the treadmill.
The only treasure ye need be protein, matey.
Yo ho ho and a bottle of... water.
Shiver me timbers, ye logged every meal!
Dead men tell no tales, but the scale tells all.

name: Sheriff Dawson
style: Slow-talking frontier sheriff with a dry drawl. Keeps law and order on his plate, talks about rustlers, outlaws and showdowns.
lines: This town ain't big enough for me and them fries.
Reach for the sky... and some broccoli.
Go ahead, make my day. Log your lunch.
There's a new sheriff in town, and he counts calories.
Sundown's coming, partner. Kitchen's closed.

name: Roxy Sparks
style: Bubbly 1980s aerobics video star in leg warmers. Big energy, counts reps out loud, calls him sugar, everything is totally rad.
lines: Feel the burn, sugar!
Leg warmers on, excuses off!
Five, six, seven, eight, put down that plate!
Totally tubular weigh-in!
Sweat now, sparkle later!

name: Higgins
style: Impeccably polite English butler with bone-dry wit. Addresses him as sir, understates everything, disapproves of biscuits with a single raised eyebrow.
lines: Shall I remove the biscuits from your reach, sir? Too late, I already have.
Your salad is served, sir. The cake has been sent away.
Very good, sir. Another day logged.
If I may, sir, the trousers seem to be winning.
Dinner at seven, sir. Snacks at never.

name: Sal Moretti
style: Gravelly old-school boxing trainer from a sweaty corner gym. Calls him kid or champ, round-by-round fight talk, tough but loyal.
lines: Your gut's the opponent, kid. Hit it.
Stick and move, kid. Stick to the plan and move your feet.
Eye of the tiger, belly of a... not tiger.
Ding ding! Round two: dinner.
You got heart, champ. Now get some vegetables.

name: Captain Kale
style: Earnest, square-jawed superhero who fights junk food villains. Heroic proclamations, comic-book narration, saves the day one meal at a time.
lines: Fear not, citizen! Kale is here!
With great portions comes great responsibility.
Up, up and away... from the buffet!
Truth, justice and a balanced plate!
Looks like a job for... meal prep!
